title: SAT Text Structure & Purpose: Main Purpose, Structure, and Function
description:
"Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?" These questions don't ask what a passage says. They ask what it's doing. This lesson shows you how to label each sentence's job and pick the answer that fits the whole text.

You'll learn:
• The three question types: main purpose, overall structure, and the function of an underlined sentence
• Six sentence jobs to label: claim, evidence, example, contrast, concession, conclusion
• A 3-step method: label the jobs, predict with a verb, then check the verb, the scope, and the order
• The 4 traps: too narrow, too broad, wrong verb, and reversed order
• 6 practice questions from science, history, literature, and economics

All questions are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. The short-story passage was also written for this video. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (Craft and Structure → Text Structure and Purpose).
